sections.label: Three parts of Bill
sections.summary: The Bill covers a new licensing regime for FTZ operators, new regulations on cargo handlers and agents, and amendments to customs enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The first is a new licensing regime on the operators of our FTZs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The second relates to new regulations on cargo handlers and other cargo agents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: And the third involves amendments to the enforcement powers of the Director-General (DG) and officers of customs under the revised Act.

sections.label: Licensing regime for privatised entities
sections.summary: A licensing regime is more fit-for-purpose since these entities have been privatised.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: As these entities have since been privatised, a licensing regime is more fit-for-purpose.

sections.label: Powers of Director-General and Customs
sections.summary: The DG of Customs may grant, renew, suspend or revoke licences, impose conditions, and order removal or detainment of goods, with Customs officers given entry, inspection, investigation, arrest and search powers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The DG of Customs will be allowed to grant, renew, suspend or revoke licences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: He or she will also be empowered to impose or modify licensing conditions and order the removal of dangerous goods, as well as the detainment of goods for Customs' inspection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The Bill will also introduce powers for officers of Customs to enter any area within the FTZ and inspect or remove goods within the FTZ.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: They will also be empowered to request for information for the purposes of investigation, witness examination, arrest of any person without warrant and search of any arrested person.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: These powers are necessary to allow Customs, as the FTZ regulator, to ensure the compliance of FTZ operators, cargo handlers, cargo agents and other entities and persons operating within the FTZs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The remaining amendments to the Bill are operational and administrative in nature, such as amendments to the penalty framework to address non-compliance with the licensing framework and to allow for compoundable offences in lieu of prosecution.

sections.label: FTZ operators licensed by DG
sections.summary: FTZs will be managed by FTZ operators licensed by the DG of Customs, with Jurong Port, PSA Corporation and Changi Airport Group continuing to manage the 10 FTZs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One of the main changes appears to be that the FTZs will no longer be managed by authorities that are answerable to the Minister but, instead, by FTZ operators who will be licensed by the DG of Customs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, I understand that the same three authorities – Jurong Port, PSA Corporation and Changi Airport Group – will continue to manage the 10 FTZs as FTZ operators.

sections.label: Cargo information disclosure duties
sections.summary: FTZ cargo handlers must disclose certain cargo information to the licensed FTZ operator, who must disclose the same information to the DG of Customs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The amended Act will also require FTZ cargo handlers to disclose certain cargo information to the licensed FTZ operator in a prescribed form, manner and timeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In turn, the FTZ operator owes a duty to disclose the same information to the DG of Customs in order to facilitate enforcement of the Act.

sections.label: DG power to prohibit entry
sections.summary: Section 10 confers powers on the DG to prohibit a person from entering or residing in an FTZ.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Section 10 confers powers to the DG to prohibit a person from entering or residing in an FTZ.

sections.label: FTZ suspicious goods reporting
sections.summary: New section 14N requires FTZ operators and cargo handlers to report suspicious goods.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The new section 14N compels FTZ operators and cargo handlers to submit reports on suspicious goods.

sections.label: Suspension notice effective date
sections.summary: Section 14P(6) states a DG suspension, revocation or regulatory action takes effect from notice service or a specified date.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Section 14P(6) stipulates that a decision by the DG to suspend or revoke an operational licence or to impose a regulatory action takes effect from the date on which the notice is served, or any other date as specified in the notice.

sections.label: Contraventions and FTZ operator numbers
sections.summary: Questions ask how many Act contraventions were raised to Customs in five years, how flagged, and how many FTZ operators and handlers exist and will be licensed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, in the past, how many contraventions of the Act have been raised to Customs over the past five years and have these instances been flagged by the operators themselves or was it because of tip-offs that were received by the authorities?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Relatedly, how many FTZ operators and handlers currently operate in our FTZs and how many are expected to be licensed by the Government under the new legislation?

sections.label: Trade decline and deglobalisation
sections.summary: International goods trade never fully recovered after the Global Financial Crisis as a share of global GDP, prompting deglobalisation claims.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: International trade in goods never quite recovered after the collapse in the aftermath of the Global Financial Crisis, at least as a share of global Gross Domestic Product (GDP), prompting some to declare that globalisation has reached its peak and others to even pronounce that we are now in the new phase of "deglobalisation".

sections.label: International minimum corporate tax
sections.summary: International minimum corporate tax and BEPS agreements progress slower but remain on track, weakening Singapore's crude tax competition advantages.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, agreements on an international minimum corporate tax, base erosion profit shifting (BEPS), while progressing at a slower pace, nevertheless remain on track for roll-out over the next few years, which will similarly weaken some of the advantages that Singapore has enjoyed in terms of attracting global capital through crude tax competition.

sections.label: FTZ role and Bill doubts
sections.summary: Changing FTZ nature may relegate this work, so while supporting the Bill, questions remain over whether it achieves its objectives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, the changing nature of FTZs in the global economy may yet relegate our work here to a back seat, at least from the perspective of long-term economic performance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, while I support the Bill, nagging questions over whether it will truly make substantial headway in fulfilling the objectives it purports to achieve, nevertheless remain.

sections.label: FTZ private entity appointment criteria
sections.summary: Asks what conditions and criteria are stipulated for appointing the private entities designated to oversee the 10 FTZs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, with regard to the various entities designated to oversee the 10 FTZs, as they are private entities, what are the stipulated conditions and criteria for their appointment?

sections.label: Powers delegated to DG
sections.summary: Raises concern about the Minister delegating greater powers to the DG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, the delegation of greater powers to the DG by the Minister is a point of concern.

sections.label: Data accuracy assurance mechanisms
sections.summary: Asks what mechanisms will be used to ensure the accuracy of the data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can we get insights into the mechanisms that will be employed to ensure the accuracy of this data?

sections.label: FTZ data disclosure to INTERPOL
sections.summary: Asks whether FTZ data will be disclosed to foreign law enforcement agencies like INTERPOL without explicit consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will data collected within FTZs be disclosed to foreign law enforcement agencies, such as INTERPOL, without the explicit consent of the individuals or entities involved?

sections.label: FATF FTZ money laundering risks
sections.summary: States FATF finds FTZs vulnerable to trade-based money laundering and says the amendment adds checks and a stronger framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Financial Action Task Force, or FATF, FTZs are vulnerable to trade-based money laundering through the misrepresentation of the price, quantity or quality of imports and exports, phantom shipments and falsification of invoices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my view, this amendment removes legal uncertainty by creating security measures that ensure that goods passing through Singapore follow very stringent checks enforced by FTZ authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe this amendment also provides a stronger framework for preventing money laundering and financing for terrorism.

sections.label: Customs officers investigation powers
sections.summary: States the amendment gives Customs and Excise Department officers more powers to investigate and arrest suspected illegal activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, the proposed amendment provides more powers to the officers of the Customs and Excise Department to investigate and arrest any parties suspected of illegal activity.

sections.label: SMEs adjustment period needed
sections.summary: SMEs will need a longer period to adjust to the main tenets of the new amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SMEs will require a longer period to adjust to the main tenets of the new amendments.

sections.label: Global free trade zones
sections.summary: There are over 3,500 to over 5,000 FTZs in more than 135 countries, boosting economic opportunities, foreign direct investments and job creation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Depending on your sources, there are now over 3,500 to over 5,000 FTZs in more than 135 countries around the world, boosting economic opportunities, foreign direct investments and job creation, in particular, by offering exemptions from duty and taxes and simplified administrative procedures and less regulations.

sections.label: FTZ amendments align with practices
sections.summary: The proposed amendments align with international best practices and clarify regulations on FTZ control and responsibilities of Customs, operators, cargo handlers and shipping agents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments have sought to align with international best practices, taking into account industry practices here and provide good clarity regarding regulations covering the control of the FTZs and the division of responsibilities of the various players, including Customs, the FTZ operators who will now be licensed, the FTZ cargo handlers and shipping agents.

sections.label: FTZ operators report suspicious activities
sections.summary: Licensed FTZ operators and cargo handlers must report suspicious activities and goods to Customs, similar to the financial sector's reporting obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Licensed FTZ operators and cargo handlers are also obligated to report to Customs suspicious activities and goods in their possession, custody, charge or control that are brought or intended to be brought into Singapore or are manufactured in an FTZ and brought or intended to be brought into Singapore, in contravention of the Act or any other written law, akin to how the financial sector – as we spoke about a lot yesterday – is obligated to report suspicious transactions.

sections.label: Review of financial penalties
sections.summary: A question asks whether there is intent to review provisions on financial penalties currently capped at $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Is there an intent to review the provisions to see if the financial penalties, currently capped at $10,000, are adequate?

sections.label: Regulating FTZ cargo handlers
sections.summary: Regulating FTZ cargo handlers strengthens service standards, security, screening, tenant management and sub-leasing, and requires accurate timely cargo information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: By regulating the FTZ cargo handlers to comply with the FTZ Act, we can further strengthen service standards, security and assist authorities in detaining goods for inspection and reporting goods that have contravened any written law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is reasonable to screen any person who intends to operate in the FTZ, enhance the management of FTZ tenants and better manage sub-leasing premises in the FTZ.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: As the volume of cargo that FTZ operators handle is immense, the authorities must be given accurate and timely cargo information.

sections.label: FTZ requirements and business costs
sections.summary: The question asks how new FTZ requirements will affect business costs and FTZ competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, given the new FTZ requirements, how will this affect the overall business costs and competitiveness of our FTZs?

sections.label: FTZ regulations and business costs
sections.summary: Enhanced FTZ regulations may streamline processes long term but could immediately raise business costs through structures, security and data provision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While the enhanced regulations for FTZ operators may streamline processes in the long term, the immediate implication for businesses is a possible rise in costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Specifically, the need to construct and maintain dedicated structures, ensure heightened security measures and provide a steady stream of data to Customs can be daunting, both logistically and financially.

sections.label: FTZ regime costs and support
sections.summary: The question asks whether the revised FTZ regime will raise time costs, reduce competitiveness, and prompt fiscal support measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Will the revised FTZ regime inadvertently increase business and operational time costs and, by doing so, diminish the competitiveness of our FTZs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Will the Government introduce fiscal support measures to enable businesses to adhere to this amendment Bill and improve competitiveness?

sections.label: Amendments balance governance and business
sections.summary: The proposed amendments seek to balance better governance with preserving a pro-business environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The proposed amendments seek to strike the right balance between better governance and preserving our pro-business environment.

sections.label: Phased implementation and transitional period
sections.summary: The revised Act's provisions will be phased in from early 2024, with clauses 25 and 27 providing a six-month transitional period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Implementation of the provisions under the revised Act will be phased in from early 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As part of this, clauses 25 and 27 of the Bill provide for a six-month transitional period to allow companies time to adjust.

sections.label: Cargo data confidentiality provisions
sections.summary: Cargo data collected by Customs will be subject to new section 16A confidentiality provisions consistent with other data protection laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: All cargo data collected by Customs will be subject to the data confidentiality provisions in the new section 16A of the FTZ Act, which are consistent with our other laws pertaining to data protection and secrecy.

sections.label: FTZ operator licence validity
sections.summary: The FTZ operator licence is valid for five years and can be renewed after that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The FTZ operator licence will be valid for five years, after which, it can be renewed.

sections.label: Licence suspension or revocation
sections.summary: Licensees who wilfully and repeatedly fail to comply with licensing conditions or FTZ Act provisions may have their licence suspended or revoked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Licensees who wilfully and repeatedly fail to comply with the licensing conditions or provisions of the FTZ Act may have their licence suspended or revoked.

sections.label: Appeals against penalties
sections.summary: Appeals against any penalties imposed are provided for in section 18 of the FTZ Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Appeals against any penalties imposed are provided for in section 18 of the FTZ Act.

sections.label: World Bank logistics ranking
sections.summary: The World Bank's Logistics Performance Index (2023) placed Singapore first in almost all categories, including customs and border management, trade-related infrastructure and timeliness of shipments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The World Bank’s Logistics Performance Index (2023), which ranks countries’ performance on trade logistics, placed Singapore first in almost all categories, including customs and border management, trade-related infrastructure and timeliness of shipments.

sections.label: Formalising amendments into law
sections.summary: The amendments are to be formalised into law to put Singapore on a stronger footing to combat illicit trade and remain a critical node in global trade flows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Today, we seek to formalise these amendments into law and, in doing so, put Singapore on a stronger footing to combat illicit trade and remain a critical node in global trade flows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This will help Singapore to safeguard our position as a global trade hub in the years ahead.

sections.label: Le Freeport status
sections.summary: Le Freeport is not a free trade zone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Le Freeport is not a free trade zone.

sections.label: Global supply chain reconfiguration
sections.summary: The world is going through a reconfiguration of supply chains, as explained in an earlier response.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: First, as I explained in my earlier response, the world is going through a reconfiguration of supply chains.

sections.label: Singapore growth or stagnation
sections.summary: This would affect whether Singapore is a growth area or a stagnant area, with hardware capacity needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This would then have an impact on whether in Singapore, this would be a growth area or this would be a stagnant area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I think the hardware part is clear: we need the capacity, T5, Tuas Port.

sections.label: Singapore as trusted hub
sections.summary: People see Singapore as a reliable, trusted hub, and the FTZ Bill enhances that strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: People are now looking at Singapore and saying that "this is a place that we can rely on, this is a trusted hub".

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, I see what we are doing here – the FTZ Bill – as an enhancement of that strategy because we are cautiously optimistic about the future of trade in Singapore and the importance of connectivity to our economy.
